evidence.detail: The exact base-to-target diff was inspected. Changed paths are README.md, auth.py, issue/handoff/review/status records, server.py, tests, and web assets.
Diff whitespace validation completed successfully with exit status 0.

The unit-test command discovered 32 tests. Twenty-three completed, but all nine server integration tests errored because the read-only review sandbox prohibited binding a loopback socket; command exit status was 1.
The compile check could not write __pycache__ in the read-only checkout and exited 1 with Operation not permitted.
The governance validator could not create its temporary directory in the read-only environment and exited 1.

The committed handoff and issue table claim out-of-band success for py_compile, 32 tests, and governance validation, but no independently runnable or immutable command transcript for the exact target was available in this review environment.

evidence: Expected: logout/cancellation must clear any pending handle, and a newer start must supersede an older start, including overlapping requests, per acceptance criteria 5 and 8.
Observed: AuthManager.start performs the transport call before acquiring _lock at auth.py:160-169. It then installs its session unconditionally at auth.py:169-183.

Consequently, logout invoked while a start transport call is in flight can return and clear state, after which the stale start installs a new pending session. Likewise, if two starts overlap and the older request finishes last, the older invocation supersedes the newer one.
The added concurrency test only covers logout during poll; test_single_concurrency_supersedes runs starts sequentially, so neither start race is exercised.
findings.remediation: Add a lifecycle generation or start-request identity reserved under the lock before network I/O. Increment/invalidate it on every start and logout, and install a returned device-code session only if that request is still current. Add deterministic tests for logout during an in-flight start and for two overlapping starts completing in reverse order.
findings.title: In-flight start can undo logout or supersede a newer start
findings.verification: Use a blocking fake transport and threads/events: (1) pause start, call logout, release start, and verify no active handle/token remains; (2) pause the first start, complete the second, then release the first and verify only the second handle is current. Rerun the complete test, compile, and governance commands against the repaired commit.

limitations: Required execution evidence is incomplete: the test suite exited 1 because loopback binding is prohibited, py_compile exited 1 because bytecode output is prohibited, and governance validation exited 1 because no writable temporary directory is available.
The 23 non-server tests completed before the nine environment-caused errors, but unittest does not provide a passing result for the required full suite.
No live Microsoft sign-in was performed. This is a protected action and is explicitly not an ISSUE-0002 completion prerequisite.
Browser interaction and actual server startup could not be exercised because the review environment prohibits socket binding.
Per the binding and repository review rules, failed or unavailable required checks prohibit PASS regardless of committed author claims.
review.summary: Review is blocked by unavailable required execution evidence. Static review also found a required concurrency defect: AuthManager.start performs network I/O before establishing lifecycle ownership, so a stale in-flight start can recreate a session after logout or overwrite a newer start.
